findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookup
findings.body: When tenants use overlapping or guessable document IDs, `getDocument` now discards `ctx.tenantId`, and `loadDocument` queries only by `documentId`. This removes the existing tenant boundary and can return another tenant’s document, causing an authorization bypass and cross-tenant data disclosure.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body: Consumers importing `readCached` from `src/cache.ts` will fail to resolve or compile because the exported module was deleted. This contradicts the stated goal of preserving existing contracts; retain the export or provide a compatible replacement.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
In a shared database where tenants can have the same `documentId`, querying only by `documentId` can return another tenant’s document. Requests no longer propagate `ctx.tenantId`, breaking tenant-state isolation and causing cross-tenant data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
`ctx.tenantId` is no longer included in the database query. If two tenants share a `documentId`, `getDocument` can return another tenant’s document, causing cross-tenant data exposure. The changed two-argument signature also breaks existing typed callers of `loadDocument(db, tenantId, documentId)`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks compilation or module resolution for any existing consumer or test importing `readCached` from that module, despite the PR’s contract-preservation requirement.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in the document lookup
findings.body:
`getDocument` no longer applies `ctx.tenantId`, so any tenant that knows or guesses another tenant’s document ID can retrieve that document from the shared database, causing a cross-tenant authorization bypass and data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the tenant predicate to prevent cross-tenant query fan-out
findings.body:
When document IDs are tenant-local or the database is partitioned/indexed by tenant, this query now scans or returns matches across every tenant. I/O, result size, network traffic, and memory can grow linearly with tenant count instead of remaining tenant-bounded.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
